  • Method Details

    • configureDynamicTemperatureControl

      public void configureDynamicTemperatureControl(double designMassFlow, double designInletTemperature, double designOutletTemperature, double coolingMediumTemperature, String temperatureUnit)
      Configures a bounded dynamic cooler model driven by the equipment controller output.

      The controller output is interpreted as cooling-utility valve opening in percent. Heat-transfer effectiveness is represented by an NTU model scaled by valve opening and inverse process mass flow. This provides a reusable first-order dynamic model for control studies without requiring a fully specified utility-side stream.

      Parameters:
      designMassFlow - design process mass flow in kg/hr
      designInletTemperature - design process inlet temperature
      designOutletTemperature - design process outlet temperature
      coolingMediumTemperature - cooling-medium supply temperature
      temperatureUnit - temperature unit shared by the three temperature arguments

    • runTransient

      public void runTransient(double dt, UUID id)
      runTransient This method calculates thermodynamic and unit operations using difference equations if available and calculateSteadyState is true. Use setCalculateSteadyState to set the parameter. Sets calc identifier UUID.

      Steady-state equipment may be evaluated repeatedly with the same calculation identifier while a transient solver refines one physical timestep. Every evaluation still calls SimulationInterface.run(UUID), but the equipment clock advances only for the first successful evaluation of a non-null identifier. For a null identifier, every successful evaluation advances the clock. The default transient boundary does not set an identifier in that case, so any identifier mutation performed by run(null) is retained.

      Specified by:
      runTransient in interface SimulationInterface
      Overrides:
      runTransient in class Heater
      Parameters:
      dt - Delta time [s]
      id - Calculation identifier
